items.title: N. Chandrababu Naidu sworn in as AP Chief Minister (4th term)
items.sum: TDP-led NDA alliance (TDP, Jana Sena, BJP) won the 2024 AP Assembly election; Naidu took oath on 12 June 2024 at Kesarapalli, near Gannavaram. Pawan Kalyan became Deputy CM.
bg: Election held together with Lok Sabha polls on 13 May 2024; results on 4 June 2024.
NDA won 164 of 175 Assembly seats; TDP won 135.
YSRCP, the previous ruling party, was reduced to 11 seats.
Naidu's earlier terms: 1995–2004 (united AP) and 2014–2019 (residuary AP).
rel: 2014: AP bifurcation under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014; Hyderabad shared as a joint capital for up to 10 years (ended 2 June 2024).
2019: YSRCP won 151 seats, Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy became CM.
Three-capital proposal (2020) was dropped; Amaravati revived as the single capital.
ex: Prelims: Number of seats, ministers, who became Deputy CM.
Mains: Coalition politics, federalism, state finances after bifurcation.
mcq: How many Assembly seats did the TDP win in 2024?
Which article deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister?
Article 164

items.title: Amaravati capital construction restarts
items.sum: Work on the Amaravati capital city was formally relaunched in May 2025 after a gap of nearly five years, with funding support from multilateral lenders and the Centre.
bg: Amaravati was chosen as AP's capital in 2014; foundation stone laid 22 Oct 2015 at Uddandarayunipalem.
Capital region was built through land pooling by farmers, a model studied widely in planning courses.
World Bank and ADB loans plus central assistance were arranged for the first phase.
rel: 2019–24: Works stalled; three-capital plan floated, then struck down in legal challenges and withdrawn.
2024: Capital revived with Centre's backing and budget support.
ex: Prelims: Land pooling, CRDA, river on which Amaravati stands (Krishna).
Mains: Capital planning, land acquisition vs land pooling, centre–state fiscal support.
mcq: On which river bank is Amaravati located?
Krishna
Which authority governs the capital region?
AP Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA)

items.title: Polavaram Irrigation Project: status and funding
items.sum: Polavaram is a multipurpose project on the Godavari, declared a National Project under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014. Funding, rehabilitation and phase-wise completion remain recurring news.
bg: Located near Polavaram in Eluru district; planned to irrigate lakhs of acres, supply water to Visakhapatnam and generate hydropower.
Centre reimburses irrigation component costs as per its National Project status.
Issues: resettlement & rehabilitation, submergence concerns raised by Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Telangana.
rel: Section 90 of AP Reorganisation Act 2014: National Project status.
Godavari–Banakacherla and river-linking discussions link to this topic.
Polavaram–Banakacherla interlinking debates involve Krishna–Godavari water sharing.
ex: Prelims: Location, river, project type, which act gave national status.
Mains: Inter-state water disputes, rehabilitation policy, irrigation planning.
mcq: Polavaram is built on which river?
Godavari
Which act declared it a National Project?
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014

items.title: Google announces large AI data centre hub in Visakhapatnam
items.sum: Google announced a multi-billion-dollar AI hub in Visakhapatnam, described as its largest investment in India, covering data centre capacity and subsea cable links.
bg: Visakhapatnam is a cable landing hub with growing international connectivity.
The state is positioning itself for data centres and green energy.
Announced investment is widely reported at about 15 billion dollars over several years.
rel: AP's Data Centre and IT policies aim to attract global firms.
Related: Digital India, India AI Mission (2024).
ex: Prelims: City, sector, cable landing concept.
Mains: Industrial policy, digital economy and employment in AP.
mcq: Where will Google's AI hub be located in AP?
Visakhapatnam

items.title: Operation Sindoor
items.sum: India launched Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025, striking terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir after the 22 April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.
bg: Pahalgam attack killed 26 civilians, mostly tourists.
India put the Indus Waters Treaty 'in abeyance' and took diplomatic steps.
Hostilities ended with a ceasefire understanding on 10 May 2025.
rel: 2016 surgical strikes (Uri) and 2019 Balakot airstrike are earlier examples.
Indus Waters Treaty, 1960, was mediated by the World Bank.
ex: Prelims: Date, treaty names, rivers under Indus system.
Mains: Cross-border terrorism, India's doctrine, water diplomacy.
mcq: Which treaty did India hold in abeyance in April 2025?
Indus Waters Treaty, 1960

items.title: GST rate rationalisation (GST 2.0)
items.sum: From 22 September 2025, GST was largely simplified into two main slabs, 5% and 18%, with a 40% rate for a few sin and luxury goods.
bg: Decided by the GST Council, a constitutional body under Article 279A.
Earlier slabs: 5, 12, 18 and 28 per cent.
GST was launched on 1 July 2017 through the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
rel: GST Council chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
Compensation cess period ended and was being phased out.
ex: Mains: Cooperative federalism, tax simplification, revenue impact on states.
mcq: Which constitutional amendment introduced GST?
101st Amendment Act, 2016

items.title: Caste enumeration to be included in the next Census
items.sum: The Union Cabinet decided in April 2025 to include caste enumeration in the upcoming national Census, the first such full caste count since 1931.
bg: The last caste-wise Census was in 1931; SECC 2011 data was never fully released.
Census is on the Union List (Entry 69, Seventh Schedule).
The Census reference period was announced for 2027.
rel: Linked to delimitation, women's reservation (106th Amendment, 2023) and OBC sub-categorisation.
Bihar conducted its own caste survey in 2023.
ex: Prelims: Census Act 1948, Union List entry, last caste Census year.
Mains: Social justice, reservation policy, data for welfare planning.
mcq: When was the last full caste-wise Census held?

items.title: One Nation One Election Bills introduced
items.sum: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 and a companion Union Territories bill were introduced in Lok Sabha in December 2024 and sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
bg: Proposal follows the Ram Nath Kovind committee report (March 2024).
Needs constitutional amendments to Articles 83, 172 and others.
Simultaneous elections occurred in India until 1967.
rel: Law Commission and NITI Aayog have earlier discussed the idea.
Concerns: federalism, early dissolution of assemblies.
ex: Prelims: Committee chair, articles involved, amendment bill number.
Mains: Pros and cons of simultaneous elections.
mcq: Who chaired the high-level committee on simultaneous elections?
Ram Nath Kovind
